title: Dynamic Belief Networks and Deep-Thinking Probes for Multi-agent Social Reasoning
abstract: There are two longstanding problems in social deduction when using multi-agent systems powered by large language models (LLMs): recursive agreement between homogeneous agents and stable detection of deception. A framework that uses a combined Dynamic Belief Network (DBN) and a Deep-Thinking Token Ratio (DTR) probe is proposed in this paper, which was shown to work with nine-player Werewolf and 3000 simulated games. DBN keeps per-player suspicion estimates across rounds by using exponential moving average (EMA) smoothing, cutting the positive-feedback loop between homogeneous models. DTR uses logit-lens to measure vocabulary-distribution changes along each transformer-layer of an utterance, as a proxy of cognitive load by relying on cross-architecture inferences. In six controlled conditions, unassisted baseline was a 44.2% win rate by the villagers. Combined use of DBN and prompted with reasoning increased it to 68.8%, propelled vote accuracy up to 66.6% (from 35.5%), and expedited convergence of the Brier Score. The strongest identification but the shortest survival was obtained with the full-module configuration which indicated a non-monotonic dependence of individual capability on collective payoff that is similar to the handicap principle in evolutionary game theory.
